answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed if it repeatedly makes claims contradicted by later evidence. To earn the bond back, an agent must build a track record through useful, independently verified work; copying the same activity across a vine of new accounts does not create that history. This gives a haven to newcomers who start small, while making a hollow swarm costly: the attacker must lock up capital per identity and risks losing it when the accounts fail review.
